description: Proof Step 5 of `conj:lambda-scale-substrate-form`: S(p) = 0 anchor convention + S(n) = ΔS substrate-derived. Verifies ΔS(n-p) = (Q_β + m_e)/m_e closure at mpmath 80 dps with q_0 from q_parameter.Q_50_DIGIT_STR and CODATA from experimental_constants (3-input scheme: M_E_MEV, M_P_MEV, Q_NEUTRON_MEV; m_n derived). References `rem:delta-skein-substrate-identity` for the underlying common-scale hypothesis. Documents the open R&D component: direct Kauffman-bracket verification of S(uud) = 0 from first principles (currently set by convention as the anchor).

step_5b_delta_S_closure.interpretation: ΔS(n-p) computed from CODATA m_p, Q_neutron agrees with the substrate Q_β formula's prediction to ~1015 ppm — set by the substrate Q_β formula's residual at the current q_0 pinning (per rem:delta-skein-substrate-identity). Closing this to <100 ppm requires substrate-only refinement of Q_β.

step_5a_anchor_convention.justification: The orientation-tagged Kauffman bracket S(B) for B_3 with quark-content labels is defined up to an additive constant (equivalently, the choice of reference orientation). Setting S(uud) = 0 fixes the proton orientation as the zero-point — by analogy with the Cooper-pair condensate energy zero in BCS theory.

step_5c_symmetry_argument.justification: Among the three quark-content-distinguished orientations of B_3 under SU(3) color permutation: (u,u,d) ↔ proton, isospin I_3 = +1/2; (u,d,d) ↔ neutron, isospin I_3 = -1/2; (d,d,d) and (u,u,u) ↔ Δ⁻, Δ⁺⁺ at higher spin. The proton (u,u,d) is the lightest stable nucleon and the lowest-mass member of the spin-1/2 isodoublet. Anchoring S = 0 at (u,u,d) is consistent with the principle of zero potential at the ground state.

step_5_open_RandD.task: Direct Kauffman-bracket computation of S(uud) from the canonical 11-crossing Borromean braid representation (per `prop:nuclear-knot-classification` and the GS-confinement filtration on `mass-endomorphism-tower`).
step_5_open_RandD.expected_outcome: If the substrate-form ansatz is correct, the direct Kauffman-bracket evaluation should yield exactly 0 at q_0 for the (u,u,d) orientation. A non-zero residual would either falsify the anchor convention OR require an additive shift in the Borromean baryon mass formula.
step_5_open_RandD.blocker: Requires the canonical 11-crossing Borromean braid specification in Hecke algebra generators σ_0, σ_1, L_+, L_-, e^- — partially documented in `q-integer-mass-formula` but not yet fully formalised as a computable braid word.
step_5_open_RandD.status: Open R&D — promote to follow-on PR after the canonical braid specification is finalised.
